precepts.text: The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame. Paul is not saying to ignore what we need on earth; you need that to survive. Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage than delicate fare in another man's house: it is better to have your own place, no matter how humble, than to live sumptuously in somebody else's house. Be it little or much, hold thee contented. It is a miserable life to go from house to house: where thou art a stranger, thou darest not open thy mouth.
precepts.point: Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth: mortify means to deaden. Fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence: sexual sins. And covetousness, which is idolatry: because when your god is your own flesh and you want to please that and only that, it is idolatry.
precepts.why:
Was Paul saying to ignore the things we need on earth when he said “not on things on the earth”? No. Paul was not running around contradicting the Bible; that is what the elders in these Israelite camps are doing.

“The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame.” You need that to survive. “Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage, than delicate fare in another man’s house.” It is better to have your own place, brothers, no matter how messed up it is, because it is yours, than to live sumptuously in somebody else’s house.

“Be it little or much, hold thee contented, that thou hear not the reproach of thy house.” Whether you have a little or a lot, be content. “For it is a miserable life to go from house to house: for where thou art a stranger, thou darest not open thy mouth.”

So setting your affection on things above does not mean neglecting the needs of this life. It means not living to satisfy the flesh.

precepts.text: The chief things for life are simple; better a poor man's own mean cottage than delicate fare as a freeloader in another man's house.
precepts.point: Solomon's prayer is the humble spirit: give me neither poverty nor riches, feed me with food convenient for me. Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and money has pulled people out of this walk; poverty drives a man to steal. The chief things for life are simple, water, bread, clothing, and an house to cover shame, and the Most High blessed Solomon with riches because riches were not his god.
precepts.why:
“The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame. Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage, than delicate fare in another man’s house.”

The chief things for life are simple, and better a poor man's own mean cottage than delicate fare as a freeloader in another man's house. That is Solomon's spirit in Proverbs 30: give me neither poverty nor riches, feed me with food convenient for me. Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and poverty drives a man to steal and take the name of his God in vain. Keep life simple and the name is not profaned.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

precepts.why:
This is your purpose: to be an example, to be blameless, to rule your own house, to teach your wife, to teach your children and guide them. “The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame.” You’re supposed to be providing the chief things in life for your family.

If your situation ain’t right and you don’t have the money for a down payment, you might have to rent for a while, a year, and live below your means so you can save money. But you have to establish that plan and give it to them: look, we’re going to stay in this apartment for two years, we’re not eating out, we ain’t doing no extra bowling and all that, we’re going to sacrifice for these two years. Here’s my plan: we’re going to save x amount of dollars a month, and according to my calculations in 24 months we’ll have enough for a down payment on a house; I’m going to work on my credit, you work on your credit, and we’re going to get it done. That’s what a man is supposed to do: provide a vision. Then your wife can help, and you’re working together.

There’s nothing wrong with renting, but eventually strive to get your own; put things in place to get your own, brothers. It’s better for it to be yours, because the one you rent from can come in there and say, to hell with y’all, get out of here. “Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage, than delicate fare in another man’s house.” You’re saving money because you’re living in somebody else’s house, and you want to get up out of there.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

precepts.why:
“Help thy neighbour according to thy power, and beware that thou thyself fall not into the same.” You are not supposed to fall into the same situation he was in.

Years ago a brother had four dollars in his pocket, and another brother asked to borrow four dollars for chicken wings and the train. He gave him all of it, and then came asking everyone else for money because he was broke. Help him according to your power, not so that you become the one in need.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: I shall not lack. “The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame.” Brothers and sisters, understand these are the chief things in life that we all need. We all need water, we all need bread, food, we all need clothing, and an house to cover shame. Those are the four chief principal things that we need in life, and that’s what we shall not want.
